newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to issue T$13 bln NCDs on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to issue T$13 bln NCDs on Thursday.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank said on Thursday it would issue T$13 billion in two-month negotiable certificates of deposit later in the day.
Bids would close at 15.00 local time (0700 GMT), a central bank official said.
The issue coincides with a renewed bull run in Taiwan's stock market, where the index has pushed to a series of seven-year highs in recent weeks.
Wednesday was no exception, with the index notching another seven-year high close at 9,362.68.
On Thursday, the index opened up 108.25 points or 1.16 percent at 9,470.93, a seven-year intraday high.
Taiwan's overnight and short-term money rates soared into double digits in late June as investors diverted holdings into the share market.
Some investors had also liquidated their foreign exchange holdings into Taiwan dollars, bolstering the local currency and halting what had been a slow, steady devaluation.
The currency's value again has been eroding in recent days.

The central bank repeatedly issued NCDs when the index was hottest in March and April, a move widely seen as aiming to keep a lid on the loose liquidity that many experts said was fuelling the dramatic rally.
The central bank has confirmed that it was responding to the liquidity sitution but denied that it was acting directly in response to the stock market bull run.
